name: Question 3
problem:
Consider the following relation defined on the set $A=\{-1,0,2\}.$ 

$$
R=\{(-1,2),(2,-1),(0,0),(0,2)\}
$$

Select the options that make the following reasoning correct:

Since 
{{field-1}}
and
{{field-2}}, 
the relation is 
{{field-3}}.

Since 
{{field-4}}
and
{{field-5}}, 
the relation is 
{{field-6}}.
worked_solution:
First, recall the following definitions:

- A binary relation $R,$ defined on a set $A,$ is *symmetric* if for all $x,y\in A,$ we have

$$
(x,y)\in R\,⟹\,(y,x)\in R.
$$

In other words, if a pair $(x,y)$ belongs to a symmetric relation, then the pair $(y,x)$ should also be in the relation.

- A binary relation $R,$ defined on a set $A,$ is *antisymmetric* if for all $x,y\in A,$ we have

$$
(x,y)\in R\,\text{and}\,(y,x)\in R\,⟹\,x=y.
$$

In other words, only one of the pairs, either $(x,y)$ or $(y,x),$ can be in an antisymmetric relation. Note that this condition allows pairs of the form $(x,x).$

Our relation is defined on $\{0,1,2\}.$ Notice that:

- $(-1,2)\in R$ and $(2,-1)\in R.$ So, the relation is $\text{not antisymmetric}.$

- $(0,2)\in R$ and $(2,0)\notin R.$ So, the relation is $\text{not symmetric}.$

Therefore, we can conclude that the relation is neither symmetric nor antisymmetric.

Consider the following relation defined on the set A={−1,0,2}.

R={(−1,2),(2,−1),(0,0),(0,2)} Select the options that make the following reasoning correct:

Since
(−1,2)∈R

and

(2,−1)∈R
(1,1)∈R

.

EXPLANATION

First, recall the following definitions:

  • A binary relation R, defined on a set A, is symmetric if for all x,y∈A, we have (x,y)∈R⟹(y,x)∈R. In other words, if a pair (x,y) belongs to a symmetric relation, then the pair (y,x) should also be in the relation.

  • A binary relation R, defined on a set A, is antisymmetric if for all x,y∈A, we have (x,y)∈Rand(y,x)∈R⟹x=y. In other words, only one of the pairs, either (x,y) or (y,x), can be in an antisymmetric relation. Note that this condition allows pairs of the form (x,x).

Our relation is defined on {0,1,2}. Notice that:

  • (−1,2)∈R and (2,−1)∈R. So, the relation is not antisymmetric.

  • (0,2)∈R and (2,0)∉R. So, the relation is not symmetric.

Therefore, we can conclude that the relation is neither symmetric nor antisymmetric.
